patch_description: The current program (score 0.80) uses a monolithic annealing loop with a `softmin` surrogate that only smooths triangles within 5% of the minimum — a very narrow, brittle landscape. The best prior program (score 0.82) uses a multi-start pipeline: `_soft_search` (soft-min over the smallest 15% of triangles, temp=200) → `_hard_refine` → `_directed_polish` → `_pair_exchange`, with structured seeds. I adopt that pipeline wholesale and apply the recommended landscape improvement: anneal the soft-min temperature progressively (temp = 50·(1+5·it/iters), i.e. 50→300) inside `_soft_search`. A low initial temp gives a smooth, gradient-rich landscape (the near-minimal set dominates gently), while the sharpening schedule makes the surrogate converge toward the hard minimum before the Phase 2 hard refinement takes over, smoothing the soft→hard transition. This changes only the landscape geometry, not the acceptance logic (keep-if-improved), which prior generations showed is the right acceptance scheme. All seeds and the RNG are deterministic (seed 20240517), preserving reproducibility, and the try/except fallback to `_lattice_seed` provides graceful error handling.
